claim_level: C2 finite theorem; OS continuum and theory identity open

nodes.statement: H is a finite positive self-adjoint Hamiltonian with normalized zero-energy vacuum omega, and the probe family has a nonzero centered component.
The time-translation invariant observable subspace is K = direct_sum_lambda ran(P_lambda restricted to D).
The visible gap is min{lambda : P_lambda D is nonzero}; it equals the spectral gap of H restricted to K.
K is dense in omega-perp exactly when sum_lambda rank(P_lambda restricted to D) = dim(H)-1; multiplicities must be fully spanned.
A Hilbert-norm-compatible bilinear bound on a dense core extends by continuity to the full omega-perp operator norm.
For a positive self-adjoint finite Hamiltonian, ||exp(-tH)|omega-perp|| <= exp(-mt) for all t iff the true gap is at least m.
For H = diag(0,0.4,1.2), the probe e_2 reports visible gap 1.2 while the true gap is 0.4.
Seeing the lowest eigenvalue does not prove density when its eigenspace has invisible multiplicity.
T_a = diag(1,exp(-a^2)) has a positive step exponent at every cutoff but physical-time gap a tending to zero.
A reflection-positive continuum limit and its OS Hilbert space, vacuum, and Hamiltonian have been constructed.
The proposed gauge-invariant temporal probes are dense and state-separating in the reconstructed physical norm after quotienting OS null vectors.
Their connected correlations obey a cutoff-, volume-, boundary-, and history-uniform norm-compatible decay bound with positive rate in physical time.
The reconstructed algebra, vacuum sector, time normalization, and Hamiltonian are identified uniquely with four-dimensional pure Yang-Mills.
The finite H9 theorem proves the continuum Yang-Mills mass gap.

first_open_physical_implication: Prove density/state separation in the OS physical norm and a uniform positive physical-time decay estimate for the same continuum-identified temporal core.
